output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mainly a Quillbook connector problem, not a price problem. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March, and since then Crewlane's fallback route has dropped or doubled invoices. That has hit 1,212 of 1,900 connected accounts. Of those, 34% had cancelled by 31 July, against 8% of connected accounts with no recorded failure. Quillbook-connected accounts churn at about 6% a month whether they are on the new price or the locked $39 price. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, are at about 1.9%, which is flat, even at the new price and in every seat band. The earlier price pattern by account size came about because bigger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. The Tallymarsh numbers are small and look like normal variation, but nobody has reviewed that connector's log.

Next: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority, and contact every Quillbook-connected account, including those who have left, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, because it stops duplicates reaching customers' books. Do not roll back the price or start the Tallymarsh rebuild yet. Instead, have someone review the Tallymarsh log. Make the sync warnings visible on the health panel. Confidence is high, though the price effect is not fully ruled out.
